holidays.name: International Waffle Day
holidays.description: Fire up the waffle iron. This day celebrates golden, crispy, syrup-holding waffles. Top them with berries and cream, fried chicken, or whatever else you like.
holidays.origin: The day began in Sweden as Våffeldagen. It grew out of Our Lady's Day (Vårfrudagen), which falls nine months before Christmas. Over the years the name slid into the similar-sounding 'waffle day', and Swedes began eating waffles that day.
holidays.funFact: Swedes traditionally eat waffles with jam and whipped cream. The name 'Vårfrudagen' sounds a lot like 'Våffeldagen', and that wordplay is how the holiday got its start.

holidays.name: Tolkien Reading Day
holidays.description: Fans of Middle-earth pick up The Hobbit or The Lord of the Rings and read aloud, host group readings, or join in themed gatherings. Second breakfast is optional but encouraged.
holidays.origin: The Tolkien Society launched the day in 2003. March 25 was chosen because it is the date in the books when Sauron is defeated and the One Ring is destroyed at Mount Doom.
holidays.funFact: Each year the Tolkien Society gives the day a theme. Past themes have included subjects like music and nature in Tolkien's works.

holidays.name: National Lobster Newburg Day
holidays.description: A salute to a luxurious, creamy dish of lobster in a rich sauce of butter, cream, sherry and egg yolks. It is a fancy way to spend a Tuesday, or any other day.
holidays.origin: The dish is tied to Delmonico's restaurant in New York City in the 1800s. Sea captain Ben Wenberg is said to have introduced the recipe. It was first called 'Lobster à la Wenberg' and later renamed 'Newburg'.
holidays.funFact: The story goes that Wenberg and Charles Delmonico had a falling out. The dish was renamed, and the new name is 'Wenberg' with its letters scrambled.
